newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese yuan ends down vs dollar on intervention.
newsitem.headline: Chinese yuan ends down vs dollar on intervention.

text.p: The Chinese yuan ended down at a one-month low of 8.2941 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2914 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai due to intervention by the central bank, the People's Bank of China, traders said.
The close was the lowest from May 5 when the yuan ended at 8.2947. The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2915.
Dealers said the central bank was seen buying dollars in the last 15 minutes of trading to depress the local currency.
The intervention came after an upward trend in recent weeks on strong pro-yuan sentiment mainly supported by China's heavy foreign trade surplus, they said.

The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2914 and hit an intraday high of 8.2913 early in trading. It then fell slightly to move around the 8.2920 level for most of the session, hitting a sudden intraday low of 8.2990 in late trading, traders said.
Trading was more active than on Wednesday with most business done at 8.2920, traders said.
One dealer said it was the central bank's intervention that caused the yuan to close sharply lower.
"Beside the central bank action, no one else on the market could depress the yuan so sharply," he said.
A second dealer said the sudden intraday low was possibily due to follow-up speculative selling after the central bank's intervention.
He said he expected the yuan to have a technical rebound on Friday after Thursday's sharp fall.
The yuan closed almost unchanged at 7.1355 from 7.1340 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0702 from 1.0705 against the Hong Kong dollar.
